items.stem: A metallic solid sphere of radius 10.5 cm melted and recasted into smaller solid cones each of radius 3.5 cm and height 3 cm. How may cones will be made ?
items.answer:
Melting conserves volume, so the volume of the sphere equals n times the volume of one cone.
Volume of sphere = (4/3)π(10.5)³ cm³.
Volume of one cone = (1/3)π(3.5)²×3 = π(3.5)² cm³.
So nπ(3.5)² = (4/3)π(10.5)³, giving n = (4/3)×10.5×(10.5/3.5)² = (4/3)×10.5×9 = 126.
Hence 126 cones can be made.
items.section_heading: THREE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board Term-2 Delhi 2017
items.ocr: Stem transcribed exactly as printed; the book prints 'How may cones' for 'How many cones'.

items.stem: A solid sphere of diameter 6 cm is dropped in a right circular cylindrical vessel partly filled with water. The diameter of the cylindrical vessel is 12 cm. If the sphere is completely submerged into water, by how much will the level of water rise in the cylindrical vessel ?
items.answer:
The water pushed up equals the volume of the submerged sphere.
Radius of sphere = 3 cm, radius of cylinder = 12/2 = 6 cm. Let the rise in water level be h.
π(6)²h = (4/3)π(3)³
36h = (4/3)×27 = 36
h = 1 cm.
Hence the water level rises by 1 cm.

items.stem: A conical vessel, with base radius 5 cm height 24 cm, is full of water. This water emptied into a cylindrical vessel, of base radius 10 cm. Find the height to which the water will rise in the cylindrical vessel. Use π = 22/7
items.answer:
The water keeps its volume when it is poured across.
Volume of cone = (1/3)π(5)²×24 = 200π cm³.
Let the water rise to height h in the cylinder of radius 10 cm.
π(10)²h = 200π
100h = 200
h = 2 cm.
Hence the water rises to a height of 2 cm.
items.section_heading: THREE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board Term-2 OD 2016
items.ocr: The printed solution writes the cone volume line as (1/3)π × 2.5 × 24; it is a misprint for 25 (= 5²), and the rest of the solution uses 25 correctly.

items.stem: A well of diameter 4 m is dug 14 m deep. The earth taken out is spread evenly all around the well to form a 40 m high embankment. Find the width of the embankment.
items.answer:
Radius of the well = 2 m, depth = 14 m.
Volume of earth dug out = πr²h = (22/7)×2²×14 = 176 m³.
The embankment is a ring of inner radius 2 m, outer radius (2 + w) m and height 0.4 m (40 cm), where w is its width.
π[(2 + w)² − 2²]×0.4 = 176
(22/7)(w² + 4w)(0.4) = 176
w² + 4w = (176×7)/(0.4×22) = 140
w² + 4w − 140 = 0
(w + 14)(w − 10) = 0, so w = 10 (the negative root is rejected).
Hence the width of the embankment is 10 m.
items.ocr: Stem says a '40 m high embankment' but the worked solution uses a height of 0.4 m (40 cm) throughout; 40 cm is what makes the printed answer of 10 m come out, so the stem's unit is the misprint. The printed solution also labels the radius 'r = 12 m' while squaring 2 in the very next line. Both transcribed as printed; the worked answer 10 m is kept.

items.stem: A sphere of diameter 12 cm, is dropped in a right circular cylindrical vessel, partly filled with water. If the sphere is completely submerged in water, the water level into the cylindrical vessel rises by 3 5/9 cm. Find the diameter of the cylindrical vessel.
items.answer:
Radius of the sphere = 12/2 = 6 cm, so its volume = (4/3)π×6³ cm³.
The rise in water level is 3 5/9 = 32/9 cm. Let r be the radius of the cylinder.
Volume of water raised = volume of the submerged sphere:
πr²×(32/9) = (4/3)π×6³
r² = (216×3×4)/32 = 81
r = 9 cm.
Hence the diameter of the cylindrical vessel is 2r = 18 cm.

items.stem: A well of diameter 4 m dug 21 m deep. The earth taken out of it has been spread evenly all around it in the shape of a circular ring of width 3 m to form an embankment. Find the height of the embankment.
items.answer:
Radius of the well r = 4/2 = 2 m, depth = 21 m.
Volume of earth dug out = πr²d = (22/7)×2²×21 = 264 m³.
The embankment is a ring of inner radius 2 m and outer radius 2 + 3 = 5 m. Let its height be h.
π(R² − r²)h = 264
(22/7)(5² − 2²)h = 264
(22/7)(21)h = 264
66h = 264
h = 4 m.
Hence the height of the embankment is 4 m.
items.section_heading: THREE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board Term-2 Delhi 2016
items.ocr: The printed solution writes the volume of earth as 264 m² and its ring formula as π(R − r)²h, but the numbers substituted are (5² − 2²) and the unit is a volume; both are typesetting slips and the result 4 m is correct.

items.stem: A cylindrical tub, whose diameter is 12 cm and height 15 cm is full of ice-cream. The whole ice-cream is to be divided into 10 children in equal ice-cream cones, with conical base surmounted by hemispherical top. If the height of conical portion is twice the diameter of base, find the diameter of conical part of ice-cream cones.
items.answer:
Volume of the tub = πR²H = π(6)²×15 = 540π cm³, so each child gets 540π/10 = 54π cm³.
Let r be the radius of the cone. Its height h = 2 × diameter = 4r.
Volume of cone = (1/3)πr²(4r) = (4/3)πr³ and volume of hemispherical top = (2/3)πr³.
Total volume of one ice-cream = (4/3)πr³ + (2/3)πr³ = 2πr³.
So 2πr³ = 54π, r³ = 27, r = 3 cm.
Hence the diameter of the conical part is 2r = 6 cm.

items.stem: A hemispherical tank, of diameter 3 m, is full of water. It is being emptied by a pipe at the rate of 3 4/7 litre per second. How much time will it take to make the tank half empty ? Use π = 22/7
items.answer:
Radius of the tank r = 3/2 m.
Volume of the hemispherical tank V = (2/3)πr³ = (2/3)×(22/7)×(3/2)³ = 99/14 m³.
Since 1 m³ = 1000 litre, V = (99/14)×1000 litre, and half of it is (1/2)×(99/14)×1000 litre.
The pipe empties 3 4/7 = 25/7 litre per second, so if t is the time taken,
(25/7)t = (1/2)×(99/14)×1000
t = (7/25)×(1/2)×(99/14)×1000 = 990 seconds.
Hence it takes 990 s = 16 minutes 30 seconds.

items.stem: 504 cones, each of diameter 3.5 cm and height 3 cm, are melted and recast into a metallic sphere. Find the diameter of the sphere and hence find its surface area. Use π = 22/7
items.answer:
Volume of one cone = (1/3)πr²h = (π/3)×(3.5/2)²×3.
The recast sphere has the same volume as the 504 cones:
(4/3)πr³ = 504 × (π/3) × (7/4)² × 3
4r³ = 504 × (7/4) × (7/4) × 3
r³ = 126 × (7/4) × (7/4) × 3 = (7/2)³ × 27
r = 3 × 7/2 = 10.5 cm.
So the diameter of the sphere is 21 cm.
Surface area = 4πr² = 4 × (22/7) × 10.5 × 10.5 = 1386 cm².

items.stem: The 3/4 th part of a conical vessel of internal radius 5 cm and height 24 cm is full of water. The water emptied into a cylindrical vessel with internal radius 10 cm. Find the height of water in cylindrical vessel.
items.answer:
Volume of the conical vessel = (1/3)π(5)²×24 = 200π cm³, so the water in it is (3/4)×200π = 150π cm³.
Let h be the height of water in the cylinder of internal radius 10 cm.
π(10)²h = (3/4)×200π
100h = 150
h = 1.5 cm.
Hence the height of water in the cylindrical vessel is 1.5 cm.

items.stem: Rampal decided to donate canvas for 10 tents conical in shape with base diameter 14 m and height 24 m to a centre for handicapped person's welfare. If the cost of 2 m wide canvas is Rs. 40 per meter, find the amount by which Rampal helped the money.
items.answer:
Radius of a tent r = 14/2 = 7 m and height h = 24 m.
Slant height l = √(r² + h²) = √(49 + 576) = √625 = 25 m.
Curved surface area of one tent = πrl = (22/7)×7×25 = 550 m².
For 10 tents the canvas needed = 550 × 10 = 5500 m².
The canvas is 2 m wide, so its length = 5500/2 = 2750 m, and at Rs 40 per metre the cost = 2750 × 40 = Rs 110000.
Hence Rampal helped the centre with Rs 1,10,000.
items.section_heading: THREE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board Term-2 OD Compt. 2017

items.stem: A cone of maximum size is curved out from a cube edge 14 cm. Find the surface area of remaining solid after the cone is curved out.
items.answer:
The largest cone carved from a cube of edge a has base diameter a and height a, so with a = 14 cm the cone has r = 7 cm and h = 14 cm.
Slant height l = √(r² + h²) = √(49 + 196) = √245 ≈ 15.65 cm.
Surface area of the remaining solid = surface area of cube + curved surface of cone − area of the circular base removed
= 6a² + πrl − πr²
= 6×14×14 + (22/7)×7×15.65 − (22/7)×7×7
= 1176 + 22(15.65 − 7)
= 1176 + 22 × 8.65
= 1176 + 190.3
= 1366.3 cm².
items.section_heading: THREE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board Term-2 SQP 2017
items.ocr: The printed final line reads '= 1176 × 22 × 8.65 = 223792.8 cm²' — the × before 22 is a misprint for +, since the line above it is 1176 + [22(15.65 − 7)]. The solution's own derivation gives 1176 + 190.3 = 1366.3 cm², which is what is recorded. The printed solution also labels 'Height of cone h = 7 cm' while substituting 14² for the height in the slant-height step; 14 cm is correct for a cube of edge 14 cm.

items.stem: The ratio of the volumes of two spheres is 8 : 27. If r and R are the radii of sphere respectively, then find the (R − r) : r.
items.answer:
The spheres' volumes are in the ratio of the cubes of their radii:
((4/3)πr³)/((4/3)πR³) = 8/27, so r³/R³ = 8/27 and r/R = 2/3.
Taking r = 2k and R = 3k, R − r = k.
So (R − r) : r = k : 2k = 1 : 2.

items.stem: A solid cylinder of diameter 12 cm and height 15 cm is melted and recast into toys in the shape of a cone of radius 3 cm and height 9 cm. Find the number of toys formed so.
items.answer:
Cylinder: R = 12/2 = 6 cm, H = 15 cm. Cone: r = 3 cm, h = 9 cm.
Melting conserves volume, so if n toys are formed,
n × (1/3)πr²h = πR²H
n × (1/3)×3×3×9 = 6×6×15
27n = 540
n = 20.
Hence 20 toys are formed.

items.stem: Find the volume of the largest solid right circular cone that can be cut out off a solid cube of side 14 cm.
items.answer:
The base of the largest cone is the largest circle that can be inscribed in a face of the cube, and its height equals the edge of the cube.
Radius of cone r = 14/2 = 7 cm, height h = 14 cm.
Volume = (1/3)πr²h = (1/3)×(22/7)×7×7×14 = 2156/3 ≈ 718.67 cm³.
Hence the largest cone has volume 2156/3 cm³ ≈ 718.67 cm³.

items.stem: A girl empties a cylindrical bucket, full of sand, of radius 18 cm and height 32 cm on the floor to form a conical heap of sand. If the height of this conical heap is 24 cm, then find its slant height correct upto one place of decimal.
items.answer:
The sand keeps its volume, so the volume of the cone equals the volume of the cylinder. Let r₁ = 18 cm be the radius of the bucket and r₂ the radius of the heap.
(1/3)πr₂²×24 = π(18)²×32
r₂² = (3×18×18×32)/24 = 1296
r₂ = 36 cm.
Slant height l = √(h² + r₂²) = √(24² + 36²) = √(576 + 1296) = √1872 ≈ 43.3 cm.
Hence the slant height of the heap is about 43.3 cm.
items.section_heading: THREE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board Term-2 Foreign 2014
items.ocr: The printed solution ends '√1872 = 43.2 cm'; √1872 = 43.266..., which to one decimal place is 43.3 cm, so the rounded value recorded here is 43.3 cm.
